belay.P2: Either on the sizable broken ledge, or a little higher at the foot of the offwidth where both third-pitch options start.
belay.P11: At the base of the chimney, among scattered fixed pins that should be backed up.

belay.1: At the chains above the four-bolt slab; a two-bolt station also sits a few metres down and to the right of them.
belay.2: A gear belay inside the large left-facing corner.
belay.4: On a two-bolt ledge, reached by moving right across a flake after returning to the corner.
belay.7: On a large ledge, belaying from two bolts on its right side; the best stance on the route.

belay.1: A semi-hanging stance on two bolts, about 25 ft below the Lithuanian Lip.
belay.2: A semi-hanging stance on bolts, reached by following a thin crack and bolts above the Lip.
belay.3: At a bolted stance, reached after a single mandatory free move at the end of the pitch.
belay.4: On a small ledge with large bolts.
belay.5: On a small ledge with two bolts, reached by exiting right.
belay.6: On top of the Rotten Block, anchored with two bolts.
